decisions.statement: Reading one account by slug reads one index file for that slug.
Reading one account by slug opens that account's page and no other account's page.
The whole fleet is answered by one function here.
A fleet answer lists where the fleet's slugs are filed and then reads each slug's page once.
An account's slug is read off the name of that account's page file.
A fleet answer narrowed to one provider leaves out every account held elsewhere.
An account whose credential is one key is read as that key rather than as a pair.
A key asked for where the sops file holds none is answered as none.
The values observed of an account are read from the file beside that account's page.
A value is read under the key akasha declares that value as.
The old `retry-after` key is read as `retryAllowedAt`.
A rescued pair is preferred where that pair's expiry is later than the committed expiry.
A rescued pair expiring no later than the committed pair is left aside.
An account no page is filed for is answered as absent.
A sops file that will not decrypt is answered as absent.
A credential whose access-token expiry will not parse is answered as absent.
A withdrawn subscription is carried as the reason text rather than as a flag.
An account's state and that account's credential come from one reading of a page.
The repository root reaches every reader here as a parameter.
The reader of an account's secrets reaches this module as a parameter.
A caller names the account a single-account read answers about.
Every path read here sits under the root the caller hands in.
Nothing here writes.
Nothing here fetches.
Nothing here reads a clock.
Nothing here reads a root from the environment.
Nothing here decrypts.
No map of the fleet is remembered between reads.
No secret value is written to a log here.
A rescued pair spelled in kebab-case is read as a pair spelled in akasha's keys.
A fleet answer opens the page of every account listed.
An account whose page will not load is left out of a fleet answer.
A fleet credential answer decrypts the sops file beside every account listed.
An account's scopes are read as text and are matched against no declared scope.
No key is read through `text-at` here, because five readers of a key are one family.
